name: Spinnerbait Rig
rod: Medium-heavy baitcaster or medium spinning rod for smaller baits.
line: 12-17 lb mono/fluoro for bass; 30-50 lb braid with wire leader for pike/muskie.
terminal: Tie direct with improved clinch, palomar, or loop knot. Add wire leader for pike/muskie.
setup: Cast around weed edges, wood, riprap, wind-blown banks, and stained water. Retrieve steadily and bump cover when possible.
when: Best with wind, clouds, stained water, spring/fall movement, or active fish.
tips: Slow roll deeper edges in cold water

name: Bass Jig Rig
line: 12-20 lb fluorocarbon or 30-50 lb braid depending on cover.
terminal: Tie directly to jig. Add soft-plastic trailer such as craw, chunk, or swimbait.
setup: Pitch to wood, weeds, docks, rocks, riprap, and dropoffs. Let it hit bottom, then hop, drag, or swim it.
when: Good year-round, especially around cover, structure, and pressured fish.
tips: Use compact jigs in cold fronts
Match trailer action to water temperature

name: Micro Jig / Panfish Jig
terminal: 1/64 to 1/16 oz jig. Optional float 1-4 feet above jig.
setup: Cast or vertical jig near brush, weeds, docks, schools, or stocked trout cruising lanes.
when: Good for panfish and trout when fish want a small slow presentation.
tips: Tip with wax worm or tiny plastic
Use a float when fish are suspended
Slow fall often gets more bites

name: Spoon Rig
rod: Medium spinning or baitcasting rod; medium-heavy for pike/muskie.
line: 8-12 lb for trout/walleye; 15-30 lb braid or heavier for pike/muskie.
terminal: Use a snap or split ring. Add barrel swivel if line twist is an issue. Use wire leader for pike/muskie.
setup: Cast and retrieve with pauses, flutter on drops, or jig vertically near schools and structure.
when: Good around wind, baitfish, open water, harbors, points, and aggressive fish.
tips: Silver for clear water and baitfish

name: Minnow Rig
rod: Light to medium spinning rod; medium-heavy for large minnows/pike.
line: 4-8 lb for panfish/trout/walleye; heavier with leader for pike.
terminal: Hook through lips or back. Use split shot, slip float, jighead, or live-bait rig depending on depth.
setup: Fish near weed edges, brush, current seams, dropoffs, or suspended fish. Keep bait lively.
when: Good when fish are neutral, cold-fronted, or feeding on baitfish.
tips: Use slip float for precise depth

name: Worm Rig
rod: Ultralight for panfish/trout; medium for bass/catfish/carp.
line: 4-8 lb for panfish/trout; 10-20 lb for catfish/carp.
terminal: Use small hook under float for panfish; split-shot rig for trout; bottom rig for catfish/carp; Texas rig for bass plastics.
setup: Fish under a float, on bottom, or around cover depending on target species.
when: Reliable all-purpose bait when you want bites or when fish are inactive.
tips: Keep hook size matched to fish size

name: Walleye Jig Rig
rod: Medium-light or medium fast-action spinning rod.
line: 6-10 lb fluorocarbon or 10-15 lb braid with fluoro leader.
terminal: 1/16 to 3/8 oz jig depending on depth/current. Tip with minnow, crawler, leech, or soft plastic.
setup: Cast, drag, snap, or vertical jig near riprap, current seams, tailwaters, points, and dropoffs.
when: Best in low light, current, wind-blown banks, and cooler-water periods.
tips: Short hops beat big rips in cold water

name: Topwater Rig
rod: Medium or medium-heavy rod with moderate/fast action.
line: 12-17 lb mono for bass; braid with leader for heavy cover or pike.
terminal: Tie direct or use snap for walking baits. Avoid fluorocarbon because it sinks.
setup: Fish over weeds, along shade, points, calm banks, riprap, and low-light feeding areas.
when: Best early/late, cloudy days, warm water, and active shallow fish.
tips: Use walking bait on open points

name: Catfish Bottom Rig
line: 15-30 lb mono or braid; heavier around wood/current.
terminal: Slip sinker or three-way rig, swivel, 12-24 inch leader, circle hook or kahle hook.
setup: Fish cut bait, stink bait, worms, chicken liver, or live bait on bottom near current breaks, holes, wood, and evening feeding flats.
when: Best evening/night, after rain/current changes, warm water, or near scent trails.
tips: Use circle hooks and avoid hard hooksets
Fresh cut bait is excellent for channels
Live bait is better for flatheads

name: Pike/Muskie Wire Leader Rig
line: 30-80 lb braid depending on lure and fish size.
terminal: Use 9-18 inch wire or heavy fluorocarbon leader with strong snap/swivel.
setup: Pair with spoons, spinnerbaits, large minnows, swimbaits, or topwater. Fish weed edges, bays, channels, and points.
when: Any time toothy fish are possible. Especially important in pike/muskie waters.

name: Trout Float / Bottom Rig
terminal: Small hook, split shot, float for suspended fish, or sliding sinker for floating bait.
setup: Use worms, salmon eggs, small dough bait, micro jigs, or small minnows. Adjust float depth until you find cruising trout.
when: Good in stocked ponds, cool water, early season, and calm conditions.
tips: Move often until you contact fish
